# Electrical circuits: catalogue

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_catalogue.py from the code; do not edit by hand. -->

Electrical circuits by Modified Nodal Analysis: resistors, capacitors, inductors, sources and their waveforms, diodes, switches, transformers and controlled sources (Modelica Standard Library device laws); impedances, constant-power loads and power converters (Modelica Buildings Library laws); Joule heating into a thermal network; the reader of OpenModelica circuit exports. How the pieces fit together: [Electrical circuits](../applications/electrical.md).
Every application is set up the same way; see [Using noodl](../usage.md).

Import from `noodl.apps.electrical` and the modules named in each table. The full reference, with every parameter, is in the [API reference](../api.md).

## Set-up

Build the model and its starting state and inputs.

| Name | What it does | How to call it |
|---|---|---|
| `build_model`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical`</small> | Assemble the circuit model and return `(model, state, drivers)`. | `build_model(circuit, *, phasor=False, frequency=None, temperature=None, learnable=False)` |
| `initial_state`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical`</small> | The consistent initial state at time `t` (s), the start of a transient: every capacitor at its `v0`, every inductor (and transformer winding) at its `i0`, sources at their value at `t`, and the other voltages and currents consistent with those (`solve_kwargs`, such as Newton's `atol` and `rtol`, reach the layer solve). | `initial_state(model, drivers, *, t=0.0, **solve_kwargs)` |

## Network components

Descriptions of the physical objects a network is built from.

| Name | What it does | How to call it |
|---|---|---|
| `Capacitor`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical`</small> | A capacitor `i = C dv/dt` (`C` in F), with initial voltage `v0` (V). MSL `Basic.Capacitor`. | `Capacitor(name, p, n, C, v0=0.0)` |
| `Circuit`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical`</small> | A netlist: `devices` (the dataclasses of this module) between named nodes, and the `ground` node (0 V). Construction checks the device types, unique non-empty names, node names on every pin (distinct within a port), scalar parameters, waveforms, switch controls and controlled-source modes, that `ground` is a pin, and that every node is joined to `ground` through the devices' port edges (a connectivity check only: a loop of voltage sources or a cut set of current sources passes it and is refused at the solve). | `Circuit(devices, ground='0')` |
| `Conductor`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical`</small> | A linear conductance `i = G v` (`G` in S). MSL `Basic.Conductor`. | `Conductor(name, p, n, G)` |
| `ControlledSource`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical`</small> | A linear controlled source: port 1 senses (`control="voltage"`: an open circuit; `"current"`: a short) and port 2 imposes (`output="voltage"` or `"current"`) `gain` times the sensed quantity. MSL `Basic.VCV`, `VCC`, `CCV`, `CCC`. | `ControlledSource(name, p1, n1, p2, n2, gain, control, output)` |
| `CurrentSource`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical`</small> | An ideal current source `i = offset + I unit(t)` (A) entering pin `p` (flowing through the source from `p` to `n`); waveform and AC phasor as for `VoltageSource`. MSL `Sources.*Current`. | `CurrentSource(name, p, n, I, waveform=Constant(), offset=0.0)` |
| `Diode`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical`</small> | A junction diode `i = Ids (exlin(v / Vt) - 1) + v / R` (`Ids` in A, `Vt` in V, `R` the parallel leak in ohm; exponential up to `Maxexp`, linear above). MSL `Semiconductors.Diode`. Not usable in an AC analysis. | `Diode(name, p, n, Ids=1e-06, Vt=0.04, Maxexp=15.0, R=100000000.0)` |
| `IdealTransformer`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical`</small> | An ideal transformer `v1 = n v2`, `i2 = -n i1` (turns ratio `n`). MSL `Ideal.IdealTransformer` without magnetisation. | `IdealTransformer(name, p1, n1, p2, n2, n)` |
| `Inductor`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical`</small> | An inductor `v = L di/dt` (`L` in H), with initial current `i0` (A). MSL `Basic.Inductor`. | `Inductor(name, p, n, L, i0=0.0)` |
| `Resistor`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical`</small> | A linear resistor `v = R_actual i`, `R_actual = R (1 + alpha (T - T_ref))` (`R` in ohm at `T_ref` in K, `alpha` in 1/K); `T` comes from the builder's `temperature` driver, else `T = T_ref`. MSL `Basic.Resistor`. | `Resistor(name, p, n, R, alpha=0.0, T_ref=300.15)` |
| `Switch`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical`</small> | An ideal closing switch: closed `v = Ron i`, open `i = Goff v` (`Ron` in ohm, `Goff` in S); closed where its control value exceeds 0.5. `control` is a driver key (read at index 0 of its last dimension) or a `(key, index)` pair. MSL `Ideal.IdealClosingSwitch`. | `Switch(name, p, n, control, Ron=1e-05, Goff=1e-05)` |
| `Transformer`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical`</small> | Two coupled windings `v1 = L1 di1/dt + M di2/dt`, `v2 = M di1/dt + L2 di2/dt` (H), with initial currents `i0 = (i1, i2)` (A). MSL `Basic.Transformer`. | `Transformer(name, p1, n1, p2, n2, L1, L2, M, i0=(0.0, 0.0))` |
| `VoltageSource`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical`</small> | An ideal voltage source `v = offset + V unit(t)` (V), `unit` the waveform. In an AC analysis a `Sine` source is its steady-state phasor (amplitude `V`, the waveform's phase) at the analysis frequency, and a `Constant` source is the magnitude `V` at phase 0; other waveforms are refused there. MSL `Sources.*Voltage`. | `VoltageSource(name, p, n, V, waveform=Constant(), offset=0.0)` |

## Elements (constitutive laws)

The relation between the flow through an edge and the potential difference across it.

| Name | What it does | How to call it |
|---|---|---|
| `Capacitance`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical`</small> | A capacitor `q = C d(dp)/dt` (`C` in F, initial voltage `v0` in V), as companion forms: dc `q = 0`; initial `dp = v0`; phasor `q = j omega C dp`; transient backward Euler `q = C (dp - dp_prev) / dt` or trapezoidal `q + q_prev = 2 C / dt (dp - dp_prev)`. MSL `Basic.Capacitor`. | `Capacitance(C, *, v0=0.0, kind='capacitor', learnable=False)` |
| `ConstantPowerLoad`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical`</small> | A load absorbing the complex power `S = P + jQ` (W, var; positive = consumption, the power-flow convention), per edge: `q = conj(S / dp)`, on a real layer `q = P / dp`. `scale` names a driver whose per-edge values multiply `S` (a load profile). | `ConstantPowerLoad(P, Q=0.0, *, V_nominal=None, linearized=False, direct_current=False, scale=None, kind='load', learnable=False)` |
| `DependentSource`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical`</small> | A linear controlled source with edges `[control, output]` per device: the control port is an open circuit (`q1 = 0`, voltage control) or a short (`dp1 = 0`, current control), and the output port imposes `dp2` (voltage output) or `q2` (current output) as `gain` times the control voltage `dp1` or current `q1`. Default kinds `"vcvs"`, `"vccs"`, `"ccvs"`, `"cccs"`. MSL `Basic.VCV`, `VCC`, `CCV`, `CCC` (gain, transconductance in S, transresistance in ohm, current gain). | `DependentSource(gain, *, control, output, kind=None, learnable=False)` |
| `Impedance`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical`</small> | A series impedance `dp = (R + jX) q` with the reactance `X = omega L - 1/(omega C)` (`R` in ohm, `L` in H, `C` in F; `C = inf`, the default, is no capacitance) at the phasor layer's angular frequency `omega`. On a real layer (modes dc, initial, transient) it is the resistance `dp = R q`, and an edge with a reactance (`L != 0` or a finite `C`) is refused; at zero frequency an inductance is a short and a finite capacitance (an open circuit) is refused. `R = 0` is a short. Implicit (the flow is an unknown), so a zero resistance needs no special case. MBL `AC.OnePhase.Loads.Impedance`, `DC.Loads.Resistor` and the MBL short-circuit loads. `learnable` applies to `R`. Linear: valid for any phasor scaling. | `Impedance(R, *, L=0.0, C=inf, kind='impedance', learnable=False)` |
| `ImpedanceTransformer`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical`</small> | An ideal transformer behind a series primary impedance: `dp1 = Z q1 + n dp2`, `q2 = -n q1` (winding ratio `n`, primary to secondary voltage; complex primary impedance `Z` in ohm, per device). Edges `[primary node -> reference, secondary node -> reference]` per device. Phasor layers only. Linear, so valid for any phasor scaling. MBL `AC.OnePhase.Conversion.ACACTransformer` (`n = VHigh/VLow`, `Z = \|Zp\| (cos(atan(XoverR)) + j sin(atan(XoverR)))`, `\|Zp\| = VHigh^2 Zperc / VABase`). | `ImpedanceTransformer(n, impedance, *, kind='impedance_transformer')` |
| `Inductance`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical`</small> | An inductor `dp = L dq/dt` (`L` in H, initial current `i0` in A), as companion forms: dc `dp = 0`; initial `q = i0`; phasor `dp = j omega L q`; transient backward Euler `dp = L (q - q_prev) / dt` or trapezoidal `dp + dp_prev = 2 L / dt (q - q_prev)`. MSL `Basic.Inductor`. | `Inductance(L, *, i0=0.0, kind='inductor', learnable=False)` |
| `JunctionDiode`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical`</small> | A junction diode with a parallel leak: `q = Ids (exlin(dp / Vt) - 1) + dp / R`, where `exlin(x) = exp(x)` up to `Maxexp` and continues linearly above it, `exp(Maxexp) (1 + x - Maxexp)` (`Ids` saturation current in A, `Vt` voltage equivalent of temperature in V, `R` parallel resistance in ohm). With `temperature` naming a driver the current follows the junction temperature (below). MSL `Semiconductors.Diode`. Nonlinear, so not usable in a phasor layer. | `JunctionDiode(Ids=1e-06, Vt=0.04, Maxexp=15.0, R=100000000.0, *, temperature=None, N=1.0, TNOM=300.15, XTI=3.0, EG=1.11, kind='diode')` |
| `MutualInductance`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical`</small> | Two coupled windings: `dp1 = L1 dq1/dt + M dq2/dt`, `dp2 = M dq1/dt + L2 dq2/dt` (`L1`, `L2`, `M` in H; initial currents `i0 = (i1, i2)` in A, per device or shared). Companion forms as `Inductance` with the 2x2 inductance matrix. Edges `[primary, secondary]` per device. MSL `Basic.Transformer`. | `MutualInductance(L1, L2, M, *, i0=(0.0, 0.0), kind='transformer', learnable=False)` |
| `PowerConverter`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical`</small> | An AC/DC converter with a constant efficiency, in a phasor layer whose direct-current side is a complex node with zero imaginary part. Edges `[ac node -> reference, dc conductor 1 -> dc conductor 2]` per device, conductor 2 at the reference potential. Equations, with `S_ac = dp_ac conj(q_ac)` and `P_dc = Re(dp_dc conj(q_dc))` the powers into the two ports: `dp_dc = k \|dp_ac\|` (with MBL's smoothed modulus `reg_root(\|dp_ac\|^2, 1e-5)`; the imaginary part holds the DC side's at zero) and `Re S_ac + P_dc = P_loss`, `Im S_ac = 0` (unity power factor), with the loss `P_loss = (1 - eta) splice(P_dc, Re S_ac, Re q_dc, 0.1)`: a fraction of the power of whichever side feeds the converter. `k` (`voltage_ratio`) is the DC voltage over the AC root-mean-square voltage; `eta` (`efficiency`) is between 0 and 1. Valid only with root-mean-square phasors (MBL's, `S = V conj(I)`): give source amplitudes as RMS values. Phasor layers only. MBL `AC.OnePhase.Conversion.ACDCConverter` (`conversionFactor`, `eta`, `ground_DC = true`). | `PowerConverter(voltage_ratio, efficiency, *, kind='power_converter')` |
| `PrescribedCurrent`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical`</small> | An ideal current source: `q = offset + amplitude * unit(t)` (A) entering pin `p` whatever the voltage, with the waveform and its phasor as for `PrescribedVoltage`. MSL `Sources.ConstantCurrent`, `StepCurrent`, `SineCurrent`, `PulseCurrent`, `SignalCurrent`. `learnable` applies to `amplitude`. | `PrescribedCurrent(amplitude, *, waveforms=None, offset=0.0, kind='current_source', learnable=False)` |
| `PrescribedVoltage`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical`</small> | An ideal voltage source: `dp = offset + amplitude * unit(t)` (V), with `unit` the waveform (`Constant` by default; one for all edges or one per edge) evaluated at the evaluation time `t` (s). In phasor mode a `Sine(frequency, phase, start_time)` source is `dp = amplitude * exp(j (phase - omega start_time))` (peak-amplitude, sine-referenced; at the layer's frequency) and a `Constant` source is `dp = amplitude`; other waveforms are refused there. MSL `Sources.ConstantVoltage`, `StepVoltage`, `SineVoltage`, `PulseVoltage`, `SignalVoltage`. `learnable` applies to `amplitude`. | `PrescribedVoltage(amplitude, *, waveforms=None, offset=0.0, kind='voltage_source', learnable=False)` |
| `Resistance`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical`</small> | A linear resistor: `q = dp / R_actual` with `R_actual = R s (1 + alpha (T - T_ref))` (`R` in ohm at `T_ref` in K, `alpha` in 1/K); `T` (K) is read per edge from `drivers[temperature]` when `temperature` names a driver, else `T = T_ref`; `s` is read per edge from `drivers[scale]` when `scale` names a driver (a variable resistor whose resistance follows a signal), else `s = 1`. MSL `Basic.Resistor`, `Basic.VariableResistor` (its input `R` is `R s`). | `Resistance(R, *, alpha=0.0, T_ref=300.15, temperature=None, scale=None, kind='resistor', learnable=False)` |
| `SwitchedConductance`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical`</small> | An ideal closing switch: closed `q = dp / Ron`, open `q = Goff dp` (`Ron` in ohm, `Goff` in S); closed where the control value exceeds 0.5 (or is True). `control` is a driver key whose last dimension holds one value per switch edge (or one value for all), a single `(key, index)` pair read by every switch, or a sequence with one entry per edge, each a key (read at index 0) or a `(key, index)` pair. MSL `Ideal.IdealClosingSwitch`. | `SwitchedConductance(control, *, Ron=1e-05, Goff=1e-05, kind='switch')` |
| `TransformerRatio`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical`</small> | An ideal transformer without magnetisation: `dp1 = n dp2`, `q2 = -n q1` (turns ratio `n`, primary to secondary voltage). Edges `[primary p1 -> n1, secondary p2 -> n2]` per device. MSL `Ideal.IdealTransformer` with `considerMagnetization = false`. | `TransformerRatio(n, *, kind='ideal_transformer', learnable=False)` |

## Closures

Functions of the state that compute drivers each step (densities, flows, levels).

| Name | What it does | How to call it |
|---|---|---|
| `HeatedEdge`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical`</small> | A circuit device with a heat port: its edge `edge` (position in the electrical layer's `q`), its end nodes `p` and `n` (positions in `phi`), the thermal node `heat_node` of its heat port (position in the thermal layer's `phi`), and the per-edge temperature driver `temperature_key` its law reads, at position `slot` of that driver. | `HeatedEdge(edge, p, n, heat_node, temperature_key, slot)` |
| `JouleHeating`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical`</small> | A coupling closure `closure(state, drivers) -> driver updates` between a circuit layer (`electrical`) and a thermal layer (`thermal`) on one network. | `JouleHeating(heated, *, electrical='electrical', thermal='thermal', heat_key='thermal.heat', base_temperatures)` |

## Waveforms

Time signals a source follows.

| Name | What it does | How to call it |
|---|---|---|
| `Constant`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical`</small> | A constant: unit value 1 at every time (a DC source: value `offset + amplitude`). | `Constant()` |
| `Pulse`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical`</small> | A pulse train: 1 for the first `width` percent of every `period` (s) from `start_time`, else 0; `n_periods < 0` repeats for ever, otherwise the pulse train stops after `n_periods` periods (MSL `Blocks.Sources.Pulse`). | `Pulse(width, period, start_time=0.0, n_periods=-1)` |
| `Ramp`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical`</small> | A ramp: 0 before `start_time` (s), rising linearly to 1 over `duration` (s), then 1 (MSL `Blocks.Sources.Ramp`; `duration = 0` is a step). | `Ramp(duration, start_time=0.0)` |
| `Signal`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical`</small> | An external signal: the unit value is read from the driver `drivers[key][..., index]` at evaluation time (batched like any driver), so a source can follow an external input (MSL `SignalVoltage`, `SignalCurrent`). It needs no clock and has no breakpoints. | `Signal(key, index=0)` |
| `Sine`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical`</small> | A sine wave: 0 before `start_time` (s), then `sin(2 pi frequency (t - start_time) + phase)` (`frequency` in Hz, `phase` in rad; MSL `Blocks.Sources.Sine` with `continuous = false`). | `Sine(frequency, phase=0.0, start_time=0.0)` |
| `Step`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical`</small> | A step: 0 before `start_time` (s), 1 from `start_time` on (MSL `Blocks.Sources.Step`: `if time < startTime then 0 else height`). | `Step(start_time=0.0)` |

Readers and writers of other tools' file formats.

| Name | What it does | How to call it |
|---|---|---|
| `read_modelica_circuit`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical.modelica`</small> | Read a `noodl-modelica-electrical/1` file into `(model, state, drivers, names)`. | `read_modelica_circuit(path, *, substeps=1, omit=())` |

## Other classes

Supporting types.

| Name | What it does | How to call it |
|---|---|---|
| `CircuitNames`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical.modelica`</small> | What the reader built, by name. | `CircuitNames(model, times, grid, restarts, dynamic, phasor, nodes, thermal_nodes, devices, sources, columns)` |
| `Column`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical.modelica`</small> | A compared value: `part(sum(c * history[key][..., i] for i, c in terms))`, with `part` `"real"` or `"imag"` (of a phasor; the real part of a real value is itself). | `Column(key, terms, part='real')` |
| `ModelicaImportError`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical.modelica`</small> | Raised for malformed `noodl-modelica/1` JSON, or for unsupported model content. | `ModelicaImportError(...)` |

## Functions

Calculations and helpers.

| Name | What it does | How to call it |
|---|---|---|
| `ac_sweep`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical`</small> | The sinusoidal steady state of `circuit` at each of `frequencies` (Hz), one batched phasor solve: `{"frequency": (F,), "electrical.phi": (F, n), "electrical.q": (F, b)}`, complex peak-amplitude, sine-referenced phasors (`x(t) = \|X\| sin(omega t + arg X)`). `solve_kwargs`, such as `method` or Newton's `atol` and `rtol`, reach the layer solve. | `ac_sweep(circuit, frequencies, **solve_kwargs)` |
| `device_values`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical`</small> | Per device name, its `(voltage, current)` (V, A) in `state`: `v = v_p - v_n` and the current entering pin `p`, each of shape `(...,)` for a one-port device and `(..., 2)` (port 1, port 2) for a two-port device. A source delivering power has a negative current. | `device_values(model, state)` |
| `operating_point`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical`</small> | The DC operating point at time `t` (s): capacitors open, inductors shorted, sources at their value at `t` (`model.steady`; `solve_kwargs`, such as Newton's `atol` and `rtol`, reach the layer solve). On a phasor model, the AC steady state. | `operating_point(model, drivers, *, t=0.0, **solve_kwargs)` |
| `transient`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical`</small> | March the circuit over the time grid `times` (s), from `state` at `times[0]` (usually `initial_state`), one `Model.step` per interval. | `transient(model, state, drivers, times, *, integration='trapezoidal', **solve_kwargs)` |
| `extrapolate`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical.modelica`</small> | Richardson extrapolation of two `simulate` histories on the same `times`, `fine` with half the step of `coarse`, of a method of order `order`: `fine + (fine - coarse)/(2**order - 1)`. For `scheme="midpoint"` (`order=2`, symmetric, so its error expands in even powers of the step) the result is fourth order. | `extrapolate(coarse, fine, order=2)` |
| `simulate_circuit`<br><small>`noodl.apps.electrical.modelica`</small> | The circuit's history at `times` (default `names.times`; each must be a time of `names.grid`, increasing): `"time"` `(T,)` and every `".phi"` / `".q"` state entry the model returns, stacked on dim 0. | `simulate_circuit(model, state, drivers, names, *, times=None, **solve_kwargs)` |

Named values and option tables.

|---|---|
| `LAYER` | `'electrical'` |
